 Rudy Gobert (back) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Gobert is questionable with low back spasms. Joan Beringer had 12 points, seven rebounds and two blocks against the Cavaliers earlier this week and would likely start if Gobert is ruled out. 
 Joan Beringer 
 MIN 
 Forward 
 #19 
 Joan Beringer finished Monday’s loss to the Cavaliers with 12 points (6-of-6 FGs), seven rebounds and two blocked shots. 
 On a night when starting center Rudy Gobert (five points, 19 rebounds, two assists and one block) shot 0-of-8 from the field, Beringer stepped up with the fifth double-digit scoring night of his young NBA career. He was perfect from the field while also providing solid rebounding and shot-blocking. Beringer still isn’t at the point where he should be rostered in redraft leagues, but his long-term outlook is good. 
 Rudy Gobert 
 MIN 
 Center 
 #27 
 Rudy Gobert accounted for 14 points (6-of-8 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds and one assist in Friday’s win over the Magic. 
 After having just two official field-goal attempts in Wednesday’s season-opening win over the Heat, Gobert had eight on Friday. The Timberwolves center may have nights with few shots, but playing off LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards also creates opportunities for lobs. Gobert finished one rebound shy of a double-double, and providing top-100 value should not be a problem for him this season. 
 Rudy Gobert 
 MIN 
 Center 
 #27 
 Rudy Gobert amassed five points (0-of-2 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs) 15 rebounds and one assist in Wednesday’s win over the Heat. 
 Gobert took just two field-goal attempts on Wednesday, and his fantasy value came from his rebounding. One would hope the 7-footer gets more lob opportunities as the season progresses, since one of Gobert’s fantasy selling points is his high field-goal percentage. That wasn’t the case against the Heat, but that can be a challenging matchup with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on the other side. Gobert will look to be more involved offensively in Friday’s game against the Magic. 
 Joan Beringer 
 MIN 
 Forward 
 #19 
 Joan Beringer puts up 10 points, (3-of-4 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, one steal, and one block in 17 minutes against the Timberwolves. 
 If you bought low in dynasty leagues on Beringer before summer league, congratulations! He has the fantasy profile to be an impactful player in redraft and dynasty leagues going forward. If Gobert misses any time, Beringer becomes an immediate add. We might only be a year or two away before he’s a starter and putting up top 60 numbers at least. 
 Joan Beringer 
 MIN 
 Forward 
 #19 
 Joan Beringer amassed 10 points (5-of-6 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist, one steal and four blocks in Saturday’s exhibition against the Heat. 
 Rudy Gobert did not play on Saturday, opening the door for Beringer to start. The second-year center posted a stat line that included seven rebounds and four blocks, logging 24 minutes. Beringer is unlikely to play that many minutes consistently once the regular season begins. Still, with Julius Randle (Brooklyn) and Naz Reid (Charlotte) gone, he will be in the Timberwolves’ rotation. 
 Joan Beringer 
 MIN 
 Forward 
 #19 
 Joan Beringer accounted for 12 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and one blocked shot in Monday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 Is Beringer a must-draft player in standard leagues? No. However, with the Timberwolves trading Julius Randle and Naz Reid, the second-year pivot has room to earn rotation minutes behind starter Rudy Gobert. Beringer looked comfortable on the court, even attacking the Bucks’ defense off the dribble for a spinning layup in one second-half play. Redraft league managers, especially those competing in deeper leagues, should watch Beringer and his role during the preseason. 
 Joan Beringer 
 MIN 
 Forward 
 #19 
 Joan Beringer posted a double-double on Thursday with 18 points (7-of-15 FGs), 12 rebounds, one assist, one steal and four blocks against the Pelicans. 
 Beringer is a raw prospect, but after starring in summer league last year, he was able to get off to a strong start this summer. He has some growing to do before he’s ready to be an every contributor for the Timberwolves, but they’re banking on that growth happening this year. He is certainly on track to be a fantasy star one day, and he’s still only 19 years old. 
 Rudy Gobert 
 MIN 
 Center 
 #27 
 Rudy Gobert went scoreless (0-of-4 FGs) with three rebounds in Friday’s Game 6 loss to the Spurs. 
 Gobert’s matchup with Victor Wembanyama was the challenge that many expected it to be before the series began, but Game 6 was brutal. In addition to missing all four of his shot attempts, the veteran center grabbed just three rebounds and did not block a shot. The matchup at the start of the game didn’t help, either, as Gobert was assigned to guard Stephon Castle. Castle knocked down shots, scoring 14 of his game-high 32 points in the first quarter. As effective as he was in the first round, Gobert will head into the offseason with a bad taste in his mouth. Looking to 2026-27, the 7-foot-1 pivot has top-100 fantasy potential, and he can be even more valuable in roster builds that punt free-throw percentage. 
 Rudy Gobert 
 MIN 
 Center 
 #27 
 Rudy Gobert accounted for 11 points (4-of-7 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 13 rebounds, four assists and one block in Sunday’s Game 4 win over the Spurs. 
 Gobert has reached double digits in rebounds in four of his last five playoff games, with Sunday’s tally being the most for him since Game 6 of the first-round series against Denver. With Victor Wembanyama getting ejected just over three minutes into the second quarter, Gobert spent most of the night competing with Luke Kornet for rebounds and points in the paint. That won’t be the case for Game 5 on Tuesday, but the “Stifle Tower” has held his own more often than not. The winner of Tuesday’s game will take a 3-2 series lead.

 Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said Saturday that the team is being “very, very methodical” in the handling of Tobias Harris’ (calf) rehab. 
 Harris, whom the Spurs signed to a two-year deal in July, has not yet played because of a strained calf suffered during training camp. Based on Johnson’s pregame comments on Saturday, the veteran forward may not take the court for some time. “We need to just be patient and make sure we get it all the way right and get him all the way right in terms of being ready to prepare to play an NBA game at the (fast-paced) style of play we want,” Johnson said. Until then, the Spurs may not make any changes to their starting lineup as long as the current starters are healthy. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ace Bailey finished Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers with nine points (4-of-10 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist, two steals, three blocks and one three-pointer.
 Like Darryn Peterson, Bailey played the entire fourth quarter and scored five of his nine points in the period. While the offensive production was limited, the rebounds and defensive stats were good. With Jaren Jackson Jr. sidelined, the Jazz would welcome any defensive contributions from Bailey, and fantasy managers likely feel the same way.

 Darry Peterson recorded 16 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 Peterson has scored in double figures in each of Utah’s last three games. Against the Trail Blazers, he wasn’t at his best, committing three turnovers, but the rookie guard still finished with a full stat line. Peterson played the entire fourth quarter, sharing the court with Keyonte George (8/3/4/1) for seven minutes and Isaiah Collier (8/1/4/2) for the other five. According to Cleaning the Glass, Peterson has played 90% of his minutes at shooting guard thus far. That split appears unlikely to change anytime soon, which may lower his fantasy ceiling.

 Lauri Markkanen accounted for 13 points (3-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals, two blocks and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 Back on the court after missing Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with a right wrist injury, Markkanen played 29 minutes on Saturday before fouling out. Given the injury he was returning from, it wasn’t too surprising to see Markkanen shoot 2-of-11 from beyond the arc. Utah plays four games next week, starting with the Spurs on Monday. Hopefully, Markkanen is sharper than he was against Portland.
